content.title: About
content.content: Canned tomato soup is a ready‑to‑eat product made from ripe tomatoes, water, salt and spices. It is served hot and often used as a quick meal or as a base for more elaborate dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato soup is among the most popular canned foods worldwide.
Lycopene content is retained during canning, making the soup a good source of antioxidants.
Tomatoes used for the soup are frequently grown in greenhouses, ensuring a consistent flavor year‑round.
Canning allows the product to be stored for 2‑3 years without loss of taste.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: Tomato soup is low in calories, making it suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports muscle function.

items.title: Easy to prepare
items.content: Simply heat the soup in a microwave or on the stove for 5‑7 minutes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned soup can be high in salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or added spices.

items.title: BPA in packaging
items.content: Metal cans may contain traces of BPA; choose products labeled BPA‑free when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the soup until boiling, optionally add cream, herbs or croutons. It can also serve as a base for stews, pasta sauces, or risotto.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and consume within 3‑4 days, refrigerated.
